text: 3: New simplified device architecture based on stable, dopant-free spiro-OMeTAD Conventional spiro-OMeTAD hole transporting layer is a highly complex mixture as it has to be doped with various additives and dopants to oxidize pristine neutral spiro-OMeTAD (spiro0) to increase its hole conductivity. These dopants include lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI), cobalt bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (CoTFSI) salts, 4-tert-Butylpyridine, and acetonitrile. These dopants are the primary reason underlying the well-known instability issues of spiro-OMeTAD. The dopants are not only hydroscopic, but they significantly decrease the glass transition temperature of spiro-OMeTAD from 110 °C of pristine spiro-OMeTAD to ~55 °C of doped spiro-OMeTAD. This also explains the thermal instability of devices utilizing spiro-OMeTAD operated above 55 °C. Moreover, the diffusion of the Li+ and Co2+ cations towards the perovskite interface are potential reasons for many abnormal degradation behaviors experienced by devices utilizing spiro-OMeTAD, such as initial burn in and hysteresis behavior. The above disadvantages motivated us to simplify the conventional spiro-OMeTAD recipe. We first synthesized pre-oxidized spiro2+, and by precisely controlling the proportion of oxidized spiro2+ to pristine spiro0, we are able to achieve a dopant-free spiro-OMeTAD hole transporting layer that functioned without the need for any additional of the dopants mentioned above. In addition, we further incorporated ionic liquid additives based on bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide anions to tune the work function and band alignment between the spiro-OMeTAD and perovskite layer. We fabricated devices based on the regular n-i-p architecture (Figure 1(a)) incorporated with the new dopant-free spiro-OMeTAD. Three separate batches were fabricated on three different days (March 2nd, March 15th, March 21st). Figures 1(b)-(e) plot the distribution of the photovoltaic parameters of the devices. The devices were not only highly efficient, but were also reproducible batch-to-batch, with average PCEs of 25.0±0.1% (March 2nd batch), 24.8±0.3% (March 15th batch), and 24.9±0.2% (March 21st batch). The device photovoltaic parameters across the three different batches are the same within statistical uncertainty, fulfilling the goal of GNG- 2C. Furthermore, the device active area is ~10 mm2, larger than the 1 mm2 goal of the GNG. Figure 3.1. (a) Solar cell device architecture. Figure 3.2 plots the maximum power point tracking of the devices under continuous AM 1.5G illumination. The devices based on the conventional doped spiro-OMeTAD (plotted in green) have a significant initial burn-in, losing up to 15 % of its initial PCE in the first initial ~10 hours. After 200 hours, the devices retained ~80% of their initial PCE, on average. In striking contrast, the devices based on the new simplified spiro-OMeTAD (plotted in red) displayed no noticeable initial burn-in.
